- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >0.8) and forecast spikes upward, reduce the peak by 5–10% to avoid overshoot.  
- If sentiment turns negative (e.g., <0.2) and forecast remains high, lower the 30d mean by 3–5% to reflect mean reversion.  
- If recent history shows a sharp upward move (e.g., last 3–5 days >70) and forecast continues rising, add a downward correction of 2–4% in the next 5–7 days.  
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating +/–0.3) and forecast is erratic, smooth the 30d curve by averaging adjacent points to reduce noise.  
- If forecast consistently overestimates true values by >2% over 3–5 days, apply a 1–2% downward bias to future forecasts.  
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, if sentiment is neutral or slightly negative, apply a 1–3% downward adjustment to avoid overconfidence in upward trends.
